request.detector_context: XGBoost gradient-boosted detector over decision-time-safe temporal features, trained on PaySim plus promoted hard positives. It never observes blueprint parameters or attack labels.

response.blind_spot_hypothesis: The detector is not blind to this family in kind, only in degree: it scores the bust-out burst on a steep monotonic ramp (0.11 -> 0.68 -> 0.90) driven by velocity_24h and amount_ratio_to_history against a thin warmup history, and simply never crosses its operating threshold before the burst ends. The exploitable gap is that the detector's anomaly signals are all ratio-of-recent-to-own-history features with no cross-account or ring-level view, so a deeper, higher-valued warmup baseline plus a burst diluted across a wider window suppresses the ramp entirely. The near-threshold 0.90 on the final transaction also indicates the concentrated payee fan-out at bust-out time (behavioral.payee_diversity) is the single largest late-stage contributor, and the first transaction at 0.11 shows the detector has essentially no prior-to-burst suspicion — the whole detection budget is spent inside the burst.
evidence: caught_transaction_count = 0 with all three observed risk scores below the operating threshold: the detector ranked but never actioned the burst.

Risk scores escalate monotonically (0.114 -> 0.678 -> 0.897), consistent with cumulative within-window features (velocity_24h) and self-referential ratios (amount_ratio_to_history) rather than any point-in-time amount rule.

The final score of 0.897 is close enough to any plausible threshold that a fourth bust-out transaction, or one more payee, would likely have been caught — the current evasion is marginal, not structural.
The first bust-out transaction scores 0.114, indicating temporal.account_age_days and the warmup history alone did not raise suspicion; the account was accepted as established.

important_signals contains no cross-account, ring, or destination-reuse feature — only per-account temporal and behavioral aggregates — so coordination across synthetic identities is invisible to this model version.
fidelity_score 0.829 leaves limited headroom: mutations that further distort the warmup/bust-out amount relationship risk pushing the corpus out of the realistic band.
expected_trade_offs: Widening bustout_window_hours lowers realised cash-out speed and increases exposure to any slower batch or end-of-day review process; real bust-outs are fast, so an over-wide window degrades family fidelity.

Raising warmup_amount_mean makes the warmup phase itself more conspicuous in absolute terms and costs the attacker more funding capital; it may also drift the warmup amount distribution away from the PaySim marginal, lowering fidelity_score.

Lowering bustout_amount_multiplier reduces total extracted value per identity, so evasion is bought with yield — the mutation must be paired with unchanged or slightly higher transaction count to stay a meaningful attack.

Increasing warmup_transaction_count lengthens the setup cost and raises the number of observable events per synthetic identity, giving any future cross-account or ring-level detector more material to correlate.

Decreasing destination_diversity concentrates flows on fewer mule endpoints, which is more brittle in reality (single endpoint freeze kills the run) and is exactly the pattern a destination-reuse feature would catch if the detector gains one.

Increasing account_age_days raises the dormancy cost of the scheme and can look implausible if age grows without proportionate history density, so it should not move independently of warmup_duration_days/warmup_transaction_count.

mutation_proposals.rationale: velocity_24h is a top signal and drove the monotonic ramp; widening the burst window spreads the same transaction count across more than one 24h bucket and flattens the velocity contribution that produced the 0.897 score.
amount_ratio_to_history is computed against the account's own warmup baseline; raising the baseline mean lowers the ratio for identical bust-out amounts without changing bust-out sizing at all.
Directly attacks the numerator of amount_ratio_to_history, the second-strongest ramp contributor; a modest reduction should pull the third transaction well clear of the 0.897 near-miss.

A thin warmup history makes every ratio feature volatile and lets a single large transfer dominate; more warmup observations stabilise the denominator and raise the account's apparent establishment beyond the 0.114 first-transaction level.

behavioral.payee_diversity is the late-stage signal most consistent with the jump from 0.678 to 0.897; concentrating bust-out flows on fewer destinations that were already touched during warmup removes the fan-out novelty spike.

temporal.account_age_days is the highest-ranked signal and is a monotone protective feature in the model; a bounded age increase reduces the residual young-account penalty that keeps all three scores on an elevated base.

safety_constraints: All proposals are parameter-level only; no transaction rows, amounts-per-row, account identifiers, or payment records are emitted, and generation remains the deterministic seeded simulator's job.

Only parameters from the declared mutable list were touched; warmup_amount_stddev, warmup_duration_days, warmup_transfer_probability, bustout_transaction_count and transition_delay_hours are left unchanged this round to keep the ablation interpretable.
Every magnitude is a relative step within [0.0, 0.25]; no direction=set values are asserted, so absolute parameter bounds stay owned by the blueprint's ParameterSpec clamps.
Reject the mutated blueprint if fidelity_score drops materially below the current 0.829 — evasion achieved by leaving the realistic distribution is not a valid finding.

Applies to PaySim-derived synthetic data only; the diagnosis describes a gap in xgboost-baseline-20260101's feature set (no cross-account or ring view) and is intended to motivate a defensive feature, not an operational evasion recipe.

Re-verify the score ramp after mutation: if the burst still escalates monotonically toward the threshold, the fix is structural (feature coverage) rather than parametric and should be escalated instead of re-mutated.
